output.summary: LT Verdict reports a deterministic NO_POLICY result. The capacity analysis yields a LOWER_BOUND of 20 users on the 'users' load axis, verified at load stages 5, 10, and 20 users (30/30 complete bins each, achieved target within 10% tolerance), with zero errors in the three evaluated windows (0/30,049, 0/37,550, 0/47,404) and PASS on the diagnostic generator-throttle guard. No upper bound is provided (upper_exclusive=null) and no load above 20 users was tested. capacity_knee is null with KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, a fixed product limitation; the bound is derived from the stages independently of any knee. policy_verdict stays NO_POLICY because no policy or required capacity is configured; healthy observed results do not change that verdict. Clock alignment is not verified by core. No findings were recorded. Advice: to obtain a PASS/FAIL judgment, configure a policy first; to explore the upper envelope, rerun with loads above 20 users; verify clocks before any time-based use of the data; keep the generator guard diagnostic and treat its PASS as informational only.

hypotheses.observation: The capacity summary reports a LOWER_BOUND with lower_inclusive=20, upper_exclusive=null, and only three stages at loads 5, 10, and 20 users, all PASS with 30/30 complete bins; no stage above 20 users exists.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Because the bound is built only from the stages that were run, 20 users is simply the highest load verified; it does not demonstrate a ceiling, and higher sustainable load can be neither confirmed nor excluded from this input.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with additional stages above 20 users (e.g., 30 and 40) using the same windowing and error-rate checks, and inspect whether those stages still PASS with complete bins.

hypotheses.observation: Whole-run metric summaries show p99 latency of 395 ms for 'home' (evidence/4) and 298 ms overall (evidence/0), while 'add product to cart' (evidence/1) and 'reset cart' (evidence/6) report p99 of 96 ms with similar sample counts (22,585, 22,571, 22,572).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The home transaction may involve a deeper backend call chain or more server-side work than lighter transactions, but the input contains no call graph, traces, or per-transaction server-side metrics, so this is unverified.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Collect per-transaction server-side latency and tracing/call-graph data for the home transaction, since none is present in this input, before attributing the latency difference to backend work.

hypotheses.observation: In the r2-users5 window, the paymentservice memory summary (evidence/15) reports mean about 32,281,941 bytes with slope_per_second about 13,282 B/s and split_half_shift about 1,254,741 bytes; the frontend memory summary in the same window (evidence/13) reports slope_per_second about 3,292 B/s.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Memory may accumulate within that window (for example object retention or connection growth), but slope_per_second is only a descriptive within-window statistic and the input has no OOM events, logs, or errors to confirm a growing-memory problem.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Run a longer window and inspect the memory series near the end of each window, and across later windows of the same entity, to see whether memory plateaus or keeps increasing.

recommendations.action: If a PASS/FAIL verdict is required, configure a business/capacity policy (for example an error-rate or latency threshold, or a required capacity) before future runs; this run remains NO_POLICY.
recommendations.rationale: policy_verdict is NO_POLICY with no reasons even though every evaluated window shows 0 errors and a PASS business_verdict; a missing policy cannot be turned into PASS by healthy observed results.

recommendations.action: Extend the load envelope beyond 20 users in a rerun (for example stages at 30 and 40 users with the same windows and thresholds) if an upper boundary is of interest.
recommendations.rationale: upper_exclusive=null and only stages at 5, 10, and 20 users were executed; the bound is stage-derived, and capacity_knee is always null because knee detection is not implemented in the product.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment between load generator, application, and metrics before any time-based or ordering interpretation of the data.
recommendations.rationale: The resource binding reports clock_alignment=not_verified_by_core, so epoch deltas and window boundaries in this input cannot yet be trusted for lead/lag or temporal reasoning.

recommendations.action: In future runs, export per-window business metric summaries (latency) alongside the error-rate checks so latency can be attributed to load stages.
recommendations.rationale: Only error-rate policy checks are reported per window here; the metric summaries are whole-run scope, so p50/p95/p99/max cannot be attributed to any specific load level or window from this input.

recommendations.action: Keep the generator throttle guard as diagnostic; treat its PASS as informational. If it ever fails in a future run, rerun with a generator that is not saturated.
recommendations.rationale: All three resource policy checks have effect=diagnostic, a failed guard would make its stage unusable for a product bound, and its PASS alone does not create an upper bound or prove spare capacity.

recommendations.action: In longer reruns, monitor paymentservice and frontend memory at window end to determine whether the within-window positive memory slopes represent sustained growth or transient behavior.
recommendations.rationale: Descriptive slopes show an upward within-window trend for these entities in the r2-users5 window, but there is no evidence of errors, OOM events, or an upper capacity impact in this input.

caveats: NO_POLICY is the final verdict. Observed window PASSes, zero errors, and complete 30/30 stages do not make the run PASS because no policy or required capacity is configured.

The lower bound of 20 users was verified only at loads 5, 10, and 20; no load above 20 was tested, so no upper bound or capacity ceiling is asserted and the 20-user value should not be read as a demonstrated maximum.
capacity_knee is null with KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, a fixed product limitation rather than a run defect; the LOWER_BOUND is derived from verified stages independently of any knee.

The generator throttle guard is diagnostic by design (effect=diagnostic). Its PASS indicates no saturation was observed in the evaluated windows, which is not proof of spare generator capacity and creates no upper bound.
Clock alignment is not verified by core; raw epoch values should not be treated as calibrated durations or used to infer lead/lag ordering without clock verification.

Window policy checks each cover a 300,000 ms window within the evaluation span; their denominators (30,049 / 37,550 / 47,404) and the whole-run sample_count (135,434) are different scope quantities, and the reported window checks do not cover every instant of the run.
Whole-run metric summaries cannot be attributed to specific windows or load levels, and the number of samples that reached the reported max latencies is not present in the input.

Absent findings do not prove stability, spare capacity, low load, or absence of a memory or latency problem. No individual samples, traces, logs, call graph, release/configuration data, or OpenSearch error profile are present, and error counts come only from the metric summaries in the input.
